problem: When the window is too narrow for two useful panes, the expanded configuration workbench and task pane are stacked and both remain incomplete.
scope: task-page disclosure, wide dual-pane geometry, intermediate single-pane switching, narrow reflow, state preservation, accessibility, and fixed-browser compatibility
baseline: At 1100px and below the open configuration panel uses 72vh while the task pane remains visible below it.
benchmarks: WAI-ARIA disclosure with aria-expanded and aria-controls
VS Code left primary sidebar with explicit visibility toggle
Material 3 adaptive list-detail and supporting-pane layouts
advantages: The current semantic disclosure, state ownership, tree and editor remain intact
Wide screens retain simultaneous task context
Intermediate screens give the active configuration workflow the full width
No new dependency or unsupported container-query runtime is required
disadvantages: Tasks are intentionally hidden while configuration is expanded at intermediate widths
Returning to tasks requires one meaningful disclosure activation
A fixed breakpoint must be derived from viable pane widths and browser-tested
limitations: Chrome 84 and Firefox 78 exclude CSS container queries as the primary mechanism
Compact widths still require explorer/editor reflow inside configuration
Drag resizing and persistent custom widths are outside this request
defects: intermediate expanded state reveals two vertically incomplete work surfaces
task content remains reachable by scrolling while configuration is active
bottlenecks: the pane switch must not unmount configuration state
hidden task content must leave visual layout and accessibility exposure
the same CSS must work in current and fixed legacy browsers

metrics.name: intermediate active panes
metrics.threshold: exactly 1 at 1000px and 760px while configuration is expanded

metrics.name: wide active panes
metrics.threshold: exactly 2 at 1440px with configuration left of tasks

hypotheses: A single active pane below the viable dual-pane width is clearer than a vertical stack of incomplete workspaces
Keeping configuration mounted while hiding the sibling task pane preserves drafts and run state
A legacy-compatible media query expresses the adaptive strategy without a component dependency
allowed_variables: task pane visibility in expanded intermediate state
responsive workspace documentation and interaction contract

stages.output: failing assertions for one-pane focus and one-action task reveal
wide dual-pane and intermediate single-pane CSS

stages.rollback: unsupported CSS or state transition owner

hard_gates: known stacked intermediate baseline is rejected
expanded intermediate state exposes configuration but not tasks
one toggle activation exposes tasks at full available width
configuration state survives collapse and reopen
wide and compact layouts retain zero horizontal overflow
current and fixed browser gates pass
failure_fixtures: 1000px open workspace renders configuration above a visible task pane
task pane retains a positive bounding box while the intermediate config pane is active
success_fixtures: 1000px and 760px render only the expanded configuration pane
one toggle activation reveals a full-width task pane
390px reflows explorer above editor without overflow
fault_injections: remove task-pane suppression from the open intermediate state
hide the configuration component by unmounting it
replace the legacy media query with a container-query-only rule
rollback: Return to the earliest failing oracle, layout or compatibility owner and invalidate dependent browser evidence.

iteration_budget.review_trigger: second failure of the pane ownership model or any fixed-browser regression

stop_conditions: failure baseline rejected and current UI accepted
all accessibility, responsive and state-preservation gates pass

promotion_decision.reason: Adaptive dual-pane to focused single-pane transitions recur across operator workbenches.

writeback: Keep LocalFlow breakpoints in the project Skill and add the generic focused-pane adaptive pattern to the user-root interaction catalog.
